docs.title: get_model()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def get_model() -> str:

Description: Resolves and returns the normalized Gemini model identifier configured for the current runtime execution. The function retrieves the model name from the GEMINI_MODEL environment variable, falling back to DEFAULT_GEMINI_MODEL if undefined, and strips Google-specific resource path prefixes such as models/ or publishers/google/models/ using gemini_model_id.

Parameters: None.

Returns: * str: The sanitized model name suitable for SDK client invocation (e.g., "gemini-3.1-pro", "gemini-2.5-flash").

Raises: None.

Example: 

def get_model() -> str:
    """GEMINI_MODEL without a 'models/' or 'publishers/google/models/' resource prefix."""
    return gemini_model_id(os.getenv("GEMINI_MODEL") or DEFAULT_GEMINI_MODEL)
The implementation delegates directly to gemini_model_id defined in utils.llm_config. It ensures that resource qualifiers provided in environment variables or configuration files do not cause lookup failures when passed to the client SDK's underlying RPC methods.

docs.title: get_model_limits()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def get_model_limits(model: str) -> tuple[int, int]:

Description: Retrieves the maximum context input token limit and output token limit for a designated Gemini model. It maintains an in-memory dictionary cache (_model_limits_cache) to prevent redundant lookups. If the model limits are not cached, it initializes defaults from GEMINI_DEFAULT_LIMITS. When operating against Google AI Studio (indicated by the absence of GEMINI_PROJECT_ID), it attempts an active API inquiry via _get_client().models.get(model=model) to inspect runtime token bounds. If Vertex AI is active or the API query raises an exception, the lookup degrades safely to static limit mappings.

Parameters: * model (str): The normalized model identifier whose limits are being queried.

Returns: * tuple[int, int]: A 2-tuple containing (input_token_limit, output_token_limit).

Raises: None. Exceptions raised during API metadata calls are caught and emitted as diagnostic warnings.

Example: 

def get_model_limits(model: str) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """(input_token_limit, output_token_limit). AI Studio reports them via models.get; Vertex does
    not (the SDK maps no limits there), so the static Gemini 3.x / 2.5 table applies."""
    if model in _model_limits_cache:
        return _model_limits_cache[model]
    limits = GEMINI_DEFAULT_LIMITS
    if not os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID"):
        try:
            info = _get_client().models.get(model=model)
            limits = (getattr(info, "input_token_limit", None) or limits[0], getattr(info, "output_token_limit", None) or limits[1])
            emit_raw("DEBUG", f"Gemini models.get | model={model} | input={limits[0]:,} | output={limits[1]:,}", dest="LOG")
        except Exception as e:
            emit("WARN_GEMINI_MODEL_LOOKUP", model=model, error=str(e)[:200])
    _model_limits_cache[model] = limits
    return limits
This function utilizes an in-memory caching pattern to optimize token budgeting calls across generation phases. Because the Google Cloud Vertex AI endpoint does not expose input and output limits through the models.get SDK contract, the implementation gates the remote network call to AI Studio environments. Any network failure or unexpected payload attribute gracefully preserves the conservative default limits defined in GEMINI_DEFAULT_LIMITS.

docs.title: call_gemini()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def call_gemini(prompt: str, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:

Description: Dispatches a single-turn completion prompt to the configured Google Gemini model, processes the resultant server-sent event stream, records usage telemetry and billing estimations, and validates completion status flags.

Parameters: * prompt (str): The primary instruction and contextual content sent to the model. * thinking_level (str | None, optional): Desired reasoning intensity level ("minimal", "low", "medium", "high"), an explicit numeric budget string, or None to leverage model defaults.

Returns: * str: The fully accumulated text payload returned by the model. If generation was abruptly halted by output token ceilings, returns an instance of TruncatedResponse (a str subclass).

Raises: * LLMRefusalError: If the generation candidate or prompt was halted due to content blocking, prohibited safety categories, reciting copyrighted material, or language constraints. * genai_errors.ClientError: If a non-400 Google client error occurs or an unrecoverable API error is encountered. * ValueError: If neither GEMINI_PROJECT_ID nor GEMINI_API_KEY is present in the environment during client initialization.

docs.title: Phase 1: Request Assembly and Configuration
docs.text:
from utils.token_utils import count_tokens_raw

    model = get_model()
    raw_tokens = count_tokens_raw(prompt)
    max_output = _max_output_tokens(model, thinking_level)
    thinking, level_desc = _thinking_config(model, thinking_level)
    # No tools are passed, so automatic function calling is off (google-genai warns on streams otherwise).
    no_afc = types.AutomaticFunctionCallingConfig(disable=True)
    config = types.GenerateContentConfig(max_output_tokens=max_output, thinking_config=thinking, automatic_function_calling=no_afc)
    emit_raw(
        "DEBUG",
        f"Gemini request | model={model} | {level_desc} | max_output_tokens={max_output:,} | location={gemini_location() if os.getenv('GEMINI_PROJECT_ID') else 'ai-studio'}",
        dest="LOG",
    )
In the initial preparation phase, call_gemini measures baseline input tokens using count_tokens_raw to establish reference points for token ratios and logging. It derives the output ceiling via _max_output_tokens() and translates the requested thinking intensity into an SDK-compliant types.ThinkingConfig via _thinking_config(). To prevent unwanted console warnings emitted by google-genai when streaming responses without tool definitions, AutomaticFunctionCallingConfig(disable=True) is explicitly configured within GenerateContentConfig.

docs.title: Phase 2: Stream Execution and Self-Healing Fallback
docs.text:
start = time.time()
    try:
        result = _stream(model, prompt, config)
    except genai_errors.ClientError as e:
        # A model that rejects our thinking control (unknown future model, level set changed):
        # warn once and resend without it for the rest of the run.
        if getattr(e, "code", None) == 400 and thinking is not None and "think" in str(e).lower():
            _thinking_rejected.add(model)
            emit("WARN_GEMINI_THINKING_REJECTED", model=model, error=str(e)[:200])
            config = types.GenerateContentConfig(max_output_tokens=max_output, thinking_config=None, automatic_function_calling=no_afc)
            result = _stream(model, prompt, config)
        else:
            raise
    elapsed = time.time() - start
The execution phase delegates transport consumption to the private helper _stream. If the API returns a client error (HTTP status 400) specifically citing thinking parameters—which commonly occurs when upstream Google endpoints alter accepted thinking configurations or reject thinking configurations on newly deployed snapshots—the handler catches genai_errors.ClientError. It registers the affected model in the global _thinking_rejected set, emits a diagnostic warning, constructs a revised GenerateContentConfig stripped of thinking options, and retries the generation.

docs.title: Phase 3: Telemetry, Accounting, and Debug Logging
docs.text:
if result["usage"] is not None:
        _record(model, result["usage"], raw_tokens, level_desc, result["finish"], elapsed)
    else:
        record_usage("GEMINI", model, cost=None, measured=False)  # stream carried no usage_metadata
    if is_debug() and result["thoughts"]:
        emit_raw("DEBUG", f"THINKING SUMMARY:\n{result['thoughts']}", dest="LOG")
Once the stream concludes, telemetry processing inspects the collected usage metadata. If present, it executes _record to compute financial costs, track input/output/thinking tokens, and update token calibration metrics. In scenarios where a partial or unmeasured stream omitted usage metadata, it logs an unmeasured event to ensure accounting ledgers in llm_common.py track the occurrence. If debug logging is active and the model generated internal thought summaries, they are dumped to the debug stream.

docs.title: Phase 4: Termination Reason Evaluation and Signals
docs.text:
if result["block_reason"] or result["finish"] in _BLOCK_FINISH_REASONS:
        category = result["block_reason"] or result["finish"]
        # A blocked prompt repeats for the same input; a stop on the candidate may pass on resampling.
        retryable = not result["block_reason"] and result["finish"] in _RETRYABLE_FINISH_REASONS
        count_event("GEMINI", "refusals")
        emit("WARN_LLM_BLOCKED_RETRYABLE" if retryable else "WARN_LLM_REFUSAL", provider="Gemini", model=model, category=category)
        raise LLMRefusalError(model, category, provider="GEMINI", retryable=retryable)
    if result["finish"] in _TRUNCATION_FINISH_REASONS:
        count_event("GEMINI", "truncations")
        emit("WARN_LLM_TRUNCATED", provider="Gemini", max_tokens=f"{max_output:,}")
        return TruncatedResponse(result["text"])
    if not result["text"]:
        emit_raw("WARNING", f"Gemini response contained no text (finish_reason={result['finish'] or 'n/a'})", dest="LOG")
    return result["text"]
The final phase evaluates stream completion codes against terminal conditions. Prompt-level blockages or policy violations (such as PROHIBITED_CONTENT or BLOCKLIST) cause an immediate LLMRefusalError with retryable=False. Candidate-level finish reasons like SAFETY or RECITATION are classified as retryable, raising LLMRefusalError with retryable=True to permit higher-level nodes to resample. If the stream ended due to MAX_TOKENS, the result is wrapped in TruncatedResponse to prevent disk caching in call_llm.py.

docs.title: _timeout_ms()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _timeout_ms() -> int:

Description: Calculates the total per-request execution deadline in milliseconds for Google SDK operations. It parses the GEMINI_TIMEOUT_SECONDS environment variable (defaulting to 1,800 seconds / 30 minutes) and enforces a minimum lower bound of 30 seconds to prevent premature disconnections during extended reasoning phases.

Parameters: None.

Returns: * int: Total per-request timeout duration in milliseconds.

Raises: None. Invalid numeric values fall back to the default of 1,800.0 seconds.

Example: 

def _timeout_ms() -> int:
    """Total per-request deadline (the SDK applies it to the whole streamed response)."""
    try:
        seconds = float(os.getenv("GEMINI_TIMEOUT_SECONDS", "1800"))
    except ValueError:
        seconds = 1800.0
    return int(max(seconds, 30.0) * 1000)
Because the google-genai SDK interprets the configured HTTP timeout as the deadline for the entire streamed message rather than an idle read timeout, this helper guarantees that lengthy generations spanning several thousand thinking tokens do not abort midway through the stream.

docs.title: _get_client()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _get_client():

Description: Lazily initializes and caches a singleton instance of google.genai.Client. It evaluates the execution environment to configure either a Vertex AI client (when GEMINI_PROJECT_ID is present) or a standard Google AI Studio client (when GEMINI_API_KEY is present). It configures low-level HTTP transport parameters including overall deadlines and automated retries.

Parameters: None.

Returns: * genai.Client: A shared instance of the configured Google GenAI SDK client.

Raises: * ValueError: Raised if neither GEMINI_PROJECT_ID nor GEMINI_API_KEY is detected in the runtime environment.

Example: 

def _get_client():
    global _client
    if _client is None:
        http_options = types.HttpOptions(
            timeout=_timeout_ms(),  # milliseconds; with no timeout a stalled connection hangs forever
            # One SDK retry for transient errors; PocketFlow node retries (5 x 20 s) sit on top.
            retry_options=types.HttpRetryOptions(attempts=2, http_status_codes=[408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504]),
        )
        if os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID"):
            _client = genai.Client(vertexai=True, project=os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID"), location=gemini_location(), http_options=http_options)
        elif os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY"):
            # vertexai=False explicitly: GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI=true in the environment would otherwise
            # route the API key to Vertex AI.
            _client = genai.Client(vertexai=False, api_key=os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY"), http_options=http_options)
        else:
            raise ValueError("Either GEMINI_PROJECT_ID or GEMINI_API_KEY must be set in the environment")
    return _client
The client instantiation explicitly overrides vertexai=False when using GEMINI_API_KEY to avoid accidental routing collisions caused by ambient GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI=true environment variables. Transport options establish two automated SDK-level retry attempts covering standard transient HTTP error codes before yielding control back to application-level retry loops.

docs.title: _thinking_config()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _thinking_config(model: str, level: str | None) -> tuple[types.ThinkingConfig | None, str]:

Description: Constructs the appropriate types.ThinkingConfig object based on the model's architectural capabilities and the requested thinking level. It distinguishes between models utilizing discrete categorical levels (mode == "level") and models requiring integer token budgets (mode == "budget"), ensuring that incompatible options are never conflated into an invalid HTTP 400 payload.

Parameters: * model (str): Target model name. * level (str | None): Desired reasoning intensity level or None.

Returns: * tuple[types.ThinkingConfig | None, str]: A 2-tuple containing the constructed types.ThinkingConfig instance (or None if disabled/unsupported) and a human-readable telemetry description string.

Raises: None.

Example: 

def _thinking_config(model: str, level: str | None):
    """(ThinkingConfig | None, description). Never mixes thinking_level with thinking_budget."""
    mode, spec = gemini_thinking_mode(model)
    include = True if is_debug() else None  # thought summaries only for the debug log
    if model in _thinking_rejected:
        return None, "default (thinking config rejected by model)"
    if not level:
        # Model default thinking; with --debug still ask for summaries so they can be logged.
        return (types.ThinkingConfig(include_thoughts=True) if include and mode != "none" else None), "default"
    if mode == "level":
        effective = clamp_level(level.lower(), spec) or spec[-1]
        if effective != level.lower() and warn_once("gemini_level", model, level):
            emit("WARN_THINKING_LEVEL_CLAMPED", level=level, effective=effective, model=model)
        return types.ThinkingConfig(thinking_level=effective, include_thoughts=include), f"thinking_level={effective}"
    if mode == "budget":
        low, high, _can_disable = spec
        budget = min(max(GEMINI_THINKING_BUDGETS.get(level.lower(), 4096), low), high)
        return types.ThinkingConfig(thinking_budget=budget, include_thoughts=include), f"thinking_budget={budget}"
    if warn_once("gemini_no_thinking", model):
        emit("WARN_THINKING_NOT_SUPPORTED", model=model)
    return None, "unsupported"
This helper enforces strict boundary checks on reasoning controls. When mode == "level", it leverages clamp_level to map out-of-bounds user levels (such as xhigh or max) to supported values like high. In budget mode, token counts are constrained between low and high model limits. It also dynamically injects include_thoughts=True when the application is running in debug mode.

docs.title: _max_output_tokens()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _max_output_tokens(model: str, level: str | None) -> int:

Description: Determines the maximum permissible generation token ceiling for a given model and thinking intensity.

Parameters: * model (str): Target model name. * level (str | None): Active thinking intensity level.

Returns: * int: Maximum output token limit for the request.

Raises: None.

Example: 

def _max_output_tokens(model: str, level: str | None) -> int:
    """Per-level budget capped by the model's output limit. Gemini documents separate input and
    output limits, so output is not reduced for large prompts (input_token_budget still reserves it)."""
    _input_limit, output_limit = get_model_limits(model)
    return gemini_output_budget(level, output_limit)
Unlike architectures that dynamically contract the output budget based on prompt length, Google Gemini specifies isolated input and output token boundaries. This function queries get_model_limits(model) and delegates to gemini_output_budget in llm_config.py to calculate an output allocation tailored to the reasoning budget without subtracting prompt tokens.

docs.title: _name()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _name(value: object) -> str:

Description: Safely normalizes enum instances, dynamic objects, or strings into an uppercase alphanumeric string representation.

Parameters: * value (object): An enum member, string, or arbitrary object representing a finish or block reason.

Returns: * str: Normalized uppercase member name (e.g., "MAX_TOKENS", "SAFETY").

Raises: None.

Example: 

def _name(value) -> str:
    """Enum → 'NAME' (unknown enum members arrive as dynamic values; compare by name)."""
    return (getattr(value, "name", None) or str(value or "")).split(".")[-1].upper()
The helper insulates the adapter from upstream SDK version shifts where server responses introduce new enum values or where serialization formats yield raw strings instead of class instances. It extracts the tail segment following any period delimiter and standardizes casing.

docs.title: _price()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _price(model: str, prompt_tokens: int, cached: int, output_tokens: int, today: datetime.date | None = None) -> float | None:

Description: Calculates the estimated USD cost of an API call based on token consumption, model pricing tiers, long-context thresholds, promotional schedules, and regional hosting surcharges.

Parameters: * model (str): Model identifier. * prompt_tokens (int): Total input tokens counted. * cached (int): Subset of input tokens served via context caching. * output_tokens (int): Total output tokens (including reasoning/thinking tokens). * today (datetime.date | None, optional): Explicit date override for testing promotional pricing expiration. Defaults to datetime.date.today().

Returns: * float | None: Total calculated cost in USD, or None if the model does not match any prefix in the pricing schedule.

Raises: None.

Example: 

def _price(model: str, prompt_tokens: int, cached: int, output_tokens: int, today: datetime.date | None = None) -> float | None:
    key = next((k for k in sorted(_PRICING, key=len, reverse=True) if model.lower().startswith(k)), None)
    if key is None:
        return None
    row = _PRICING[key]
    if key in _INTRO_PRICING and (today or datetime.date.today()) <= _INTRO_PRICING_UNTIL:
        row = _INTRO_PRICING[key]
    p_in, p_out, p_cache = row[3:6] if len(row) == 6 and prompt_tokens > _LONG_CONTEXT_THRESHOLD else row[:3]
    uncached = max(prompt_tokens - cached, 0)
    cost = (uncached * p_in + cached * p_cache + output_tokens * p_out) / 1_000_000
    if os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID") and gemini_location().lower() != "global":
        cost *= _REGIONAL_UPLIFT
    return cost
Pricing resolution uses a longest-prefix match against _PRICING. For eligible Flash models, it substitutes introductory pricing if the execution date precedes _INTRO_PRICING_UNTIL (December 31, 2026). If the prompt exceeds _LONG_CONTEXT_THRESHOLD (200,000 tokens) on tiered models like Gemini Pro, the rate switches to 6-tuple pricing coordinates. Additionally, requests routed through regional Vertex AI endpoints apply a 10% multiplier (_REGIONAL_UPLIFT).

docs.title: _record()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _record(model: str, usage: object, raw_prompt_tokens: int, level_desc: str, finish: str, elapsed: float) -> None:

Description: Extracts token counts from SDK usage metadata, invokes financial calculation helpers, dispatches metrics to the shared token ledger, updates token estimation ratios, and logs granular debugging telemetry.

Parameters: * model (str): The active model identifier. * usage (object): The usage_metadata object returned on the generation stream. * raw_prompt_tokens (int): Baseline prompt token count computed prior to transmission. * level_desc (str): Telemetry description of active reasoning parameters. * finish (str): Stream finish reason string. * elapsed (float): Request latency in seconds.

Returns: * None

Raises: None.

Example: 

def _record(model: str, usage, raw_prompt_tokens: int, level_desc: str, finish: str, elapsed: float) -> None:
    prompt = getattr(usage, "prompt_token_count", 0) or 0
    candidates = getattr(usage, "candidates_token_count", 0) or 0
    thoughts = getattr(usage, "thoughts_token_count", 0) or 0
    cached = getattr(usage, "cached_content_token_count", 0) or 0
    output = candidates + thoughts  # thinking is billed as output
    cost = _price(model, prompt, cached, output)
    record_usage("GEMINI", model, input_tokens=prompt, output_tokens=output, thinking_tokens=thoughts, cache_read=cached, cost=cost)
    ratio = prompt / raw_prompt_tokens if raw_prompt_tokens else 0.0
    from utils.token_utils import observe_prompt_tokens

    observe_prompt_tokens("GEMINI", model, raw_prompt_tokens, prompt)  # prompt_token_count includes cached tokens
    emit_raw(
        "DEBUG",
        f"GEMINI USAGE | model={model} | {level_desc} | finish={finish or 'n/a'} | in={prompt:,} | out={candidates:,} | thinking={thoughts:,} | "
        f"cached={cached:,} | est_cost={'$' + format(cost, '.4f') if cost is not None else 'n/a'} | elapsed={elapsed:.1f}s | observed_token_ratio={ratio:.2f}",
        dest="BOTH",
    )
This helper treats internal reasoning tokens (thoughts_token_count) as billable output tokens in accordance with Google's billing architecture. It calls record_usage in llm_common.py to register metrics in the shared step and provider ledgers. Furthermore, it dynamically imports observe_prompt_tokens from token_utils.py to continuously calibrate the runtime ratio between raw heuristic token counts and actual Gemini BPE token counts.

docs.title: _stream()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _stream(model: str, prompt: str, config: types.GenerateContentConfig) -> dict:

Description: Consumes the generate_content_stream generator from the SDK client, iterating through chunks to accumulate text, collect thought summaries, intercept prompt feedback blocks, detect candidate termination reasons, and capture final usage metadata.

Parameters: * model (str): Target model identifier. * prompt (str): The prompt payload. * config (types.GenerateContentConfig): Fully prepared generation configuration.

Returns: * dict: A dictionary structured as: 

{
    "text": str,
    "thoughts": str,
    "finish": str,
    "block_reason": str,
    "usage": types.GenerateContentResponseUsageMetadata | None,
}

Raises: * genai_errors.ClientError: Propagated on unhandled 4xx client errors. * genai_errors.APIError: Propagated on unhandled Google remote execution failures.

Example: 

def _stream(model: str, prompt: str, config) -> dict:
    """Consume generate_content_stream; returns text, thoughts, finish, block_reason, usage."""
    text, thoughts = [], []
    finish, block_reason, usage = "", "", None
    for chunk in _get_client().models.generate_content_stream(model=model, contents=[prompt], config=config):
        feedback = getattr(chunk, "prompt_feedback", None)
        if feedback is not None and getattr(feedback, "block_reason", None):
            block_reason = _name(feedback.block_reason)
        if getattr(chunk, "usage_metadata", None) is not None:
            usage = chunk.usage_metadata
        for candidate in getattr(chunk, "candidates", None) or []:
            if getattr(candidate, "finish_reason", None):
                finish = _name(candidate.finish_reason)
            content = getattr(candidate, "content", None)
            for part in (getattr(content, "parts", None) or []) if content is not None else []:
                if getattr(part, "text", None):
                    (thoughts if getattr(part, "thought", False) else text).append(part.text)
            break  # candidate_count is 1
    return {"text": "".join(text), "thoughts": "".join(thoughts), "finish": finish, "block_reason": block_reason, "usage": usage}
The stream accumulator parses each incoming response chunk, checking for prompt-level feedback blocks before evaluating candidate parts. It routes parts marked with thought=True into a dedicated thoughts accumulator to separate internal chain-of-thought tokens from the primary response text. Candidate traversal explicitly limits inspection to the primary candidate (break), aligning with the application's single-turn contract.

docs.title: Pricing Specifications (_PRICING and _INTRO_PRICING)
docs.text:
The module defines token rate schedules as tuples representing USD per 1,000,000 tokens. Entries contain either 3 values (input, output, cached_input) or 6 values (input, output, cached_input, long_context_input, long_context_output, long_context_cached).

docs.title: Finish Reason Taxonomies
docs.text:
The module organizes Google completion codes into three distinct functional sets:

Set Name Members Semantics / Pipeline Behavior _RETRYABLE_FINISH_REASONS SAFETY, RECITATION, LANGUAGE, OTHER Sampling-dependent interruptions. Raises LLMRefusalError(retryable=True) to permit retry passes. _BLOCK_FINISH_REASONS _RETRYABLE_FINISH_REASONS + PROHIBITED_CONTENT, BLOCKLIST, SPII, IMAGE_SAFETY, IMAGE_PROHIBITED_CONTENT, IMAGE_RECITATION, IMAGE_OTHER Absolute policy rejections. Non-retryable reasons raise LLMRefusalError(retryable=False) to prevent duplicate execution. _TRUNCATION_FINISH_REASONS MAX_TOKENS Token limit ceiling reached. Returns TruncatedResponse to bypass response caching in call_llm.py.

docs.title: Stream Extraction Schema (StreamResult)
docs.text:
The internal mapping returned by _stream() aggregates chunks received across the HTTP stream:

Field Type Description text str Fully concatenated response text generated by the model. thoughts str Concatenated thought reasoning parts (collected only when debug mode is active). finish str Normalized string representation of the final candidate finish_reason. block_reason str Normalized string representation of any prompt-level block reason reported in prompt_feedback. usage types.GenerateContentResponseUsageMetadata \| None Google SDK metadata object containing token counters, or None if the stream failed to provide usage.

docs.title: Module-Level State Containers
docs.text: Variable Type Description _client genai.Client \| None Global singleton instance of the initialized Google GenAI client. _model_limits_cache dict[str, tuple[int, int]] Key-value store mapping normalized model identifiers to resolved (input_limit, output_limit) tuples. _thinking_rejected set[str] Set of model identifiers that returned an HTTP 400 rejection for thinking parameters during the active process lifecycle.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
llm_gemini.py implements structured error management to handle remote API constraints, policy interventions, and network volatility:

  • Thinking Configuration Self-Healing: When invoking newer or modified model endpoints, Google may return an HTTP 400 ClientError containing "think". The adapter catches this exception during _stream(), adds the model identifier to _thinking_rejected, logs WARN_GEMINI_THINKING_REJECTED, and automatically replays the request without reasoning configurations. Subsequent calls for that model bypass thinking injection entirely.
  • Deterministic Policy Blocks vs. Sampling Rejections: The adapter categorizes refusal codes into deterministic rejections (e.g., PROHIBITED_CONTENT, BLOCKLIST, SPII, or prompt-level block_reason) versus stochastic rejections (e.g., candidate-level SAFETY, RECITATION, LANGUAGE). Stochastic rejections raise LLMRefusalError with retryable=True, allowing caller orchestrators to retry with modified parameters, whereas deterministic rejections set retryable=False to abort immediately.
  • Truncation Defense: Generations terminated due to MAX_TOKENS are intercepted and packaged within TruncatedResponse. This informs upstream cache controllers (e.g., call_llm.py) that the output is incomplete, preventing truncated content from poisoning the disk cache (llm_cache_v2.json).
  • Transport-Level Retries and Deadlines: Transport robustness is enforced via types.HttpOptions and types.HttpRetryOptions. The SDK client is configured to automatically retry transient network failures (HTTP 408, 429, 500, 502, 503, and 504) across two attempts, bound by a 30-minute default stream deadline (_timeout_ms()).

docs.title: See Also
docs.text:
• call_llm.py — The centralized LLM gateway that routes prompts to call_gemini and checks for TruncatedResponse or LLMRefusalError.
  • llm_config.py — Provides configuration resolution, model aliasing (gemini_model_id), output token budgeting, and thinking mode classification.
  • llm_common.py — Exposes shared exception types (LLMRefusalError), truncation wrappers (TruncatedResponse), and ledger tracking utilities (record_usage, count_event).
  • token_utils.py — Manages heuristic token counting (count_tokens_raw) and ratio feedback calibration (observe_prompt_tokens).
  • thinking.py — Utility for validating and clamping requested thinking levels against supported candidate sequences.
  • output.py — Emits formatted logging, user warnings, and debug traces.

docs.title: llm_openrouter.py
docs.text:
Source: utils/llm_openrouter.py

Following the provider execution harness established in llm_gemini.py for Google's Gemini models, llm_openrouter.py serves as the execution adapter and low-level transport client for OpenRouter's OpenAI-compatible completions API. Rather than relying on hardcoded static capabilities per model, this module dynamically consults the OpenRouter remote catalog via llm_config.py to inspect model constraints, reasoning mechanisms, output ceilings, and sampling options at runtime. This catalog-driven design allows the codebase knowledge builder to dispatch prompts across hundreds of upstream model architectures (including Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, Meta Llama, and Qwen) through a single unified HTTP interface without vendor SDK bloat.

The module manages the complete lifecycle of an OpenRouter chat completion request: prompt sizing, reasoning parameter adaptation, optional application attribution headers, resilient HTTP transport, Server-Sent Events (SSE) decoding, and fine-grained usage bookkeeping. Transport operations stream chunks over SSE to prevent read timeouts during prolonged chain-of-thought phases while filtering out OpenRouter keep-alive signals. The component intercepts and parses server-side error envelopes, classifying rate limits and gateway timeouts as retryable, mapping content moderations and policy rejections into structured refusal errors, and wrapping length-truncated generations into sentinels that safeguard downstream cache integrity.

docs.title: get_model()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def get_model() -> str:

Description: Resolves and sanitizes the configured OpenRouter model identifier from the runtime process environment. It reads the OPENROUTER_MODEL environment variable, strips extraneous leading and trailing whitespace, and returns the raw string identifier. If the variable is unset or contains only whitespace, an empty string is returned, which subsequently triggers configuration assertion failures in downstream dispatchers.

Returns: * str: The sanitized model name (e.g., "anthropic/claude-3.7-sonnet", "google/gemini-2.5-pro"), or an empty string if unconfigured.

Example: 

model = get_model()
if not model:
    raise ValueError("OPENROUTER_MODEL environment variable is required")

The function reads directly from the environment to allow dynamic overrides during execution runs. Calling components verify this return value prior to initiating HTTP connection attempts or token reservations.

docs.title: build_payload()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def build_payload(prompt: str, model: str, level: str | None, prompt_tokens: int) -> tuple[dict, str]:

Description: Constructs the complete OpenAI-compatible chat completion payload dictionary tailored specifically to the upstream model's declared specifications in the OpenRouter catalog. The function resolves model capabilities via openrouter_model_info(), determines planned completion ceilings through _max_tokens(), calculates reasoning parameters through _reasoning(), and conditionally evaluates sampling parameters via _sends_temperature().

The payload construction process executes across two distinct phases:

docs.title: Phase 1: Catalog & Token Limit Resolution
docs.text:
info = openrouter_model_info(model)
max_tokens = _max_tokens(model, info, level, prompt_tokens)
reasoning, desc = _reasoning(model, info, level, max_tokens)
payload = {
    "model": model,
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
    "stream": True,
}
if max_tokens:
    payload["max_tokens"] = max_tokens
In this phase, the function looks up the model's structural metadata in the local catalog. It calculates the output token limit by subtracting prompt tokens and safety margins from the context window, and configures thinking parameters according to provider requirements. The base payload dictionary is initialized with streaming explicitly enabled ("stream": True).

docs.title: Phase 2: Reasoning & Sampling Parameter Synthesis
docs.text:
if reasoning is not None:
    payload["reasoning"] = reasoning
if _sends_temperature(model, info, reasoning):
    try:
        payload["temperature"] = float(os.getenv("OPENROUTER_TEMPERATURE", "0.7"))
    except ValueError:
        payload["temperature"] = 0.7
return payload, desc
In this phase, reasoning parameters (either an effort category or an integer token budget) are attached if supported. The helper then checks whether temperature sampling is valid for this model family and thinking state; if permitted, it parses OPENROUTER_TEMPERATURE (defaulting to 0.7) and injects it into the request dictionary alongside a diagnostic configuration string.

Parameters: * prompt (str): The complete input text prompt to be processed by the model. * model (str): The target OpenRouter model identifier. * level (str | None): The requested reasoning or thinking effort level (e.g., "low", "high", None). * prompt_tokens (int): The calibrated estimate of input prompt tokens used to enforce context ceiling constraints.

Returns: * tuple[dict, str]: A 2-tuple containing: 1. dict: The serialized JSON payload ready for submission to /v1/chat/completions. 2. str: A human-readable diagnostic description of active reasoning parameters (e.g., "effort=high", "reasoning.max_tokens=8192", or "default").

Example: 

payload, desc = build_payload(
    prompt="Explain the AST architecture",
    model="anthropic/claude-3.7-sonnet",
    level="high",
    prompt_tokens=1542,
)

docs.title: call_openrouter()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def call_openrouter(prompt: str, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:

Description: The primary entry point for executing single-turn prompts via the OpenRouter API. It orchestrates preflight validation, token calibration, payload construction, resilient network transport, SSE stream aggregation, usage accounting, and termination classification. The function enforces robust error checking, raising LLMRefusalError on provider moderation rejections or policy blocks, and returning TruncatedResponse instances when generations hit max token cutoffs.

The execution workflow is structured into four distinct sequential phases:

docs.title: Phase 1: Environment & Token Preflight
docs.text:
from utils.token_utils import count_tokens_raw, token_ratio

model = get_model()
if not model:
    raise ValueError("OPENROUTER_MODEL environment variable is required")
api_key = os.getenv("OPENROUTER_API_KEY", "").strip()
raw_tokens = count_tokens_raw(prompt)  # memoized: the node already counted this prompt
payload, desc = build_payload(prompt, model, thinking_level, int(raw_tokens * token_ratio()))
The method begins by asserting the presence of OPENROUTER_MODEL. It counts raw tiktoken prompt tokens via count_tokens_raw() and scales them using token_ratio() to derive an accurate baseline for context-window clamping. It then builds the payload and extracts runtime metadata.

docs.title: Phase 2: Payload Assembly & Attribution Setup
docs.text:
headers = {"Content-Type": "application/json", **_attribution_headers()}
if api_key:
    headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {api_key}"
max_tokens = payload.get("max_tokens")
emit_raw(
    "DEBUG",
    f"OpenRouter request | model={model} | {desc} | max_tokens={f'{max_tokens:,}' if max_tokens else 'omitted'} | "
    f"temperature={payload.get('temperature', 'omitted')} | catalog={'yes' if openrouter_catalog() else 'no'} | "
    f"attribution={'on' if 'HTTP-Referer' in headers else 'off'}",
    dest="LOG",
)
Standard JSON headers are prepared alongside opt-in attribution headers generated by _attribution_headers(). If an API key is available, the Authorization bearer token header is set. Comprehensive debugging telemetry is logged before initiating network I/O.

docs.title: Phase 3: HTTP Streaming Execution & Event Consumption
docs.text:
start = time.time()
resp = _post(f"{openrouter_base_url()}/v1/chat/completions", headers, payload)
generation_id = resp.headers.get("X-Generation-Id")
result = _consume(resp)
_record(model, result, raw_tokens, desc, time.time() - start, generation_id)
if is_debug() and result["reasoning"]:
    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"REASONING:\n{result['reasoning']}", dest="LOG")
The request is dispatched through _post(), which manages transport retries and status validation. The active HTTP response is passed to _consume() to parse the SSE stream into text buffers, reasoning text, and metadata. _record() updates the central ledger, calculates token ratios, and logs latency metrics.

docs.title: Phase 4: Telemetry Recording & Response Classification
docs.text:
finish, native = (result["finish"] or ""), (result["native"] or "")
if finish == "error":
    raise RuntimeError(f"OpenRouter generation ended with an error (native_finish_reason={native or 'n/a'})")
if finish == "content_filter" or result["refusal"] or native.lower() in _REFUSAL_NATIVE_REASONS:
    category = native or finish or "refusal"
    # Filters on sampled output (safety, recitation, content_filter) may pass on another attempt.
    retryable = not result["refusal"] and native.lower() not in _DETERMINISTIC_NATIVE_REASONS
    count_event("OPENROUTER", "refusals")
    emit("WARN_LLM_BLOCKED_RETRYABLE" if retryable else "WARN_LLM_REFUSAL", provider="OpenRouter", model=model, category=category)
    raise LLMRefusalError(model, category, provider="OPENROUTER", retryable=retryable)
if not finish:
    # No data at all, or the connection dropped mid-answer: never return a partial reply.
    raise RuntimeError(
        f"OpenRouter stream ended without a finish_reason after {result['events']} events ({len(result['text']):,} characters received)"
    )
if finish == "length":
    count_event("OPENROUTER", "truncations")
    emit("WARN_LLM_TRUNCATED", provider="OpenRouter", max_tokens=f"{max_tokens:,}" if max_tokens else "default")
    return TruncatedResponse(result["text"])
if not result["text"]:
    emit_raw("WARNING", f"OpenRouter response contained no text (finish_reason={finish or 'n/a'})", dest="LOG")
return result["text"]
The final phase evaluates completion status flags. Unrecoverable stream terminations or upstream failures raise RuntimeError. Policy blocks, guardrails, and model refusals trigger LLMRefusalError (flagged as retryable if caused by stochastic sampling filters like safety or recitation). Generations terminated due to context exhaustion return a TruncatedResponse instance to protect disk caches from poisoning.

Parameters: * prompt (str): The complete text prompt dispatched to the model. * thinking_level (str | None, optional): The target reasoning effort level (e.g., "minimal", "low", "medium", "high", "max"). Defaults to None.

Returns: * str: The accumulated completion text returned by the model. May be an instance of TruncatedResponse if cut off by token limits.

Raises: * ValueError: If OPENROUTER_MODEL is missing or empty. * LLMRefusalError: If the model or gateway refuses the prompt due to policy violations, content filtering, or safety triggers. * RuntimeError: If network communication exhausts maximum retry attempts, an upstream stream error occurs, or the stream terminates prematurely without a valid finish_reason.

Example: 

from utils.llm_openrouter import call_openrouter

response = call_openrouter(
    prompt="Generate an architectural summary of utils/flow.py",
    thinking_level="medium",
)

docs.title: _read_timeout()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _read_timeout() -> float:

Description: Resolves the HTTP read timeout duration for streaming connections. It parses the OPENROUTER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS environment variable, enforcing a minimum lower bound of 30.0 seconds to prevent premature disconnections during lengthy provider reasoning phases. If the variable is unset or contains non-numeric text, it defaults to 300.0 seconds.

Returns: * float: The effective stream silence timeout in seconds (minimum 30.0).

Example: 

def _read_timeout() -> float:
    try:
        return max(float(os.getenv("OPENROUTER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS", "300")), 30.0)
    except ValueError:
        return 300.0

The function handles string parsing defensively using a try-except ValueError block. It guarantees that connection handlers receive a valid floating-point deadline even under misconfigured deployment environments.

docs.title: _reasoning()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _reasoning(model: str, info: dict | None, level: str | None, max_tokens: int | None = None) -> tuple[dict | None, str]:

Description: Adapts abstract reasoning level requests into provider-specific parameter schemas supported by OpenRouter. It parses catalog metadata to determine whether the model accepts reasoning effort strings ("effort"), explicit integer token budgets ("max_tokens"), or rejects reasoning entirely.

The helper executes across two distinct logical phases:

docs.title: Phase 1: Level Validation & Catalog Verification
docs.text:
if not level:
    return None, "default"
level = level.lower()
exclude = not is_debug()
if info is None:
    # Catalog unavailable or model unknown: send the level; OpenRouter clamps server-side.
    return {"effort": level, "exclude": exclude}, f"effort={level} (unverified)"
reasoning = info.get("reasoning")
if not isinstance(reasoning, dict) and "reasoning" not in (info.get("supported_parameters") or []):
    if warn_once("openrouter_no_reasoning", model):
        emit("WARN_THINKING_NOT_SUPPORTED", model=model)
    return None, "unsupported"
The phase verifies whether a level was requested. If the catalog is missing, it falls back to sending the unverified effort level. If the model catalog explicitly indicates that reasoning is unsupported, it logs a warning once via warn_once() and returns None.

docs.title: Phase 2: Budget-Only vs Effort-Based Parameter Assembly
docs.text:
meta = reasoning if isinstance(reasoning, dict) else {}
if "supported_efforts" not in meta and meta.get("supports_max_tokens"):
    # Budget-only model: an explicit thinking budget (OpenRouter's effort ratio of a large
    # max_tokens would over-spend). It must stay below max_tokens.
    budget = _REASONING_BUDGETS.get(level, _REASONING_BUDGETS["medium"])
    if max_tokens:
        budget = max(min(budget, max_tokens - 1_024), 1_024)
    return {"max_tokens": budget, "exclude": exclude}, f"reasoning.max_tokens={budget}"
efforts = meta.get("supported_efforts")
effort = level
if efforts:
    effort = clamp_level(level, [e for e in efforts if e != "none"]) or level
    if effort != level and warn_once("openrouter_level", model, level):
        emit("WARN_THINKING_LEVEL_CLAMPED", level=level, effective=effort, model=model)
return {"effort": effort, "exclude": exclude}, f"effort={effort}"
If the model only supports numeric token budgets (supports_max_tokens), the level is mapped to an integer budget via _REASONING_BUDGETS and clamped below max_tokens - 1024. Otherwise, effort strings are clamped against supported_efforts using clamp_level() (explicitly filtering out "none" to prevent HTTP 400 errors on mandatory-reasoning models).

Parameters: * model (str): The target model identifier. * info (dict | None): The model catalog entry returned by openrouter_model_info(). * level (str | None): The requested reasoning effort level. * max_tokens (int | None, optional): The resolved generation output ceiling. Defaults to None.

Returns: * tuple[dict | None, str]: A 2-tuple containing: 1. dict | None: The reasoning configuration dictionary (e.g., {"effort": "high", "exclude": True}) or None. 2. str: A description string for logging.

Example: 

reasoning, desc = _reasoning(
    model="anthropic/claude-3.7-sonnet",
    info={"reasoning": {"supported_efforts": ["low", "medium", "high"]}},
    level="high",
    max_tokens=16384,
)
# Returns: ({"effort": "high", "exclude": True}, "effort=high")

docs.title: _sends_temperature()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _sends_temperature(model: str, info: dict | None, reasoning: dict | None) -> bool:

Description: Determines whether the temperature parameter can safely be transmitted in the completion request. Many reasoning models (such as o1, o3, and newer Anthropic or Gemini architectures) reject sampling parameters when reasoning is enabled or mandatory. The helper disables temperature if reasoning is active, if the model family rejects sampling according to rejects_sampling_params(), if the catalog omits temperature from supported_parameters, or if reasoning is configured as mandatory or enabled by default.

Parameters: * model (str): The model identifier. * info (dict | None): The model metadata dictionary from the catalog. * reasoning (dict | None): The resolved reasoning configuration payload.

Returns: * bool: True if temperature should be included in the request payload; otherwise False.

Example: 

def _sends_temperature(model: str, info: dict | None, reasoning: dict | None) -> bool:
    if reasoning is not None or rejects_sampling_params(model):
        return False
    if info is None:
        return True
    if "temperature" not in (info.get("supported_parameters") or []):
        return False
    meta = info.get("reasoning") if isinstance(info.get("reasoning"), dict) else {}
    return not (meta.get("mandatory") or meta.get("default_enabled"))

This gatekeeper protects API calls from immediate HTTP 400 rejection errors caused by sending invalid parameter combinations to reasoning-centric backends.

docs.title: _max_tokens()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _max_tokens(model: str, info: dict | None, level: str | None, prompt_tokens: int) -> int | None:

Description: Calculates the upper limit for completion tokens (max_tokens), ensuring that the requested generation budget does not exceed the remaining capacity of the model's total context window. It queries openrouter_output_budget() for the model family's default ceiling and retrieves context length limits from the catalog metadata. If both limits are known, it clamps the planned output budget to the remaining context space minus CONTEXT_MARGIN, enforcing an absolute floor of 4,096 tokens.

Parameters: * model (str): The model identifier. * info (dict | None): The model catalog dictionary. * level (str | None): The active thinking effort level. * prompt_tokens (int): Calibrated input prompt token count.

Returns: * int | None: The clamped maximum output tokens, or None if the model or its limits are unknown.

Example: 

def _max_tokens(model: str, info: dict | None, level: str | None, prompt_tokens: int) -> int | None:
    planned = openrouter_output_budget(model, level)
    context = ((info or {}).get("top_provider") or {}).get("context_length") or (info or {}).get("context_length")
    if planned and context:
        planned = min(planned, max(context - prompt_tokens - CONTEXT_MARGIN, 4_096))
    return planned

If the catalog lacks context window data, the function returns the planned budget unmodified, leaving enforcement to OpenRouter's upstream defaults.

docs.title: _attribution_headers()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _attribution_headers() -> dict:

Description: Generates opt-in HTTP attribution headers for OpenRouter analytics and rankings. Identification headers are strictly suppressed unless the operator explicitly sets the OPENROUTER_APP_URL environment variable. When present, the function populates HTTP-Referer, X-OpenRouter-Title, and legacy X-Title headers using the internal application identity string ("Codebase Knowledge Builder").

Returns: * dict: A dictionary containing attribution headers if configured, or an empty dictionary if unset.

Example: 

def _attribution_headers() -> dict:
    url = os.getenv("OPENROUTER_APP_URL", "").strip()
    if not url:
        return {}
    return {"HTTP-Referer": url, "X-OpenRouter-Title": _APP_TITLE, "X-Title": _APP_TITLE}

This opt-in design ensures zero external telemetry or application tracking occurs during standard, unconfigured CLI executions.

docs.title: _retry_after()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _retry_after(resp: requests.Response) -> float | None:

Description: Inspects HTTP response headers for a Retry-After rate-limiting indicator. If the header exists, the helper attempts to parse it into a floating-point number representing seconds to delay before retrying. If the header is missing, empty, or unparseable, None is returned.

Parameters: * resp (requests.Response): The incoming HTTP response object.

Returns: * float | None: The delay in seconds specified by the server, or None.

Example: 

def _retry_after(resp) -> float | None:
    value = resp.headers.get("Retry-After")
    try:
        return float(value) if value else None
    except ValueError:
        return None

The function handles potential ValueError exceptions defensively to guard against malformed HTTP date stamps or non-standard header formats.

docs.title: _error_body()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _error_body(resp: requests.Response) -> dict:

Description: Safely extracts and unwraps the structured error payload from an HTTP error response. It attempts to parse the response body as JSON and resolves nested "error" keys common to OpenAI-compatible error payloads. If JSON parsing fails or the content is malformed, it gracefully returns an empty dictionary or wraps scalar messages into a standard {"message": str(err)} format.

Parameters: * resp (requests.Response): The HTTP error response.

Returns: * dict: A dictionary containing extracted error details, or an empty dictionary.

Example: 

def _error_body(resp) -> dict:
    try:
        body = resp.json()
    except ValueError:
        return {}
    err = body.get("error", body) if isinstance(body, dict) else body
    return err if isinstance(err, dict) else {"message": str(err)}

This helper prevents uncaught JSON decoding exceptions from masking the underlying HTTP transport status codes.

docs.title: _error_detail()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _error_detail(resp: requests.Response) -> str:

Description: Synthesizes a human-readable diagnostic error string from an HTTP response. It inspects the parsed payload from _error_body(), retrieving primary error messages alongside underlying provider details (such as raw error output or upstream provider identifiers). If structured error fields cannot be found, it truncates the raw response text to 300 characters.

Parameters: * resp (requests.Response): The HTTP response to inspect.

Returns: * str: A formatted error description string suitable for log output.

Example: 

def _error_detail(resp) -> str:
    err = _error_body(resp)
    if not err:
        return resp.text[:300].strip()
    meta = err.get("metadata") or {}
    raw = meta.get("raw") or meta.get("provider_name") or ""
    return f"{err.get('message', err)}" + (f" ({raw})" if raw else "")

By appending upstream provider diagnostics in parentheses, this function clarifies errors originating from specific underlying providers behind OpenRouter.

docs.title: _refusal_category()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _refusal_category(resp: requests.Response) -> str | None:

Description: Inspects an HTTP 403 Forbidden response to determine if it represents a policy violation, content moderation block, or guardrail refusal rather than an authentication failure. It checks error type identifiers against known refusal categories (_REFUSAL_ERROR_TYPES) and parses metadata reason arrays.

Parameters: * resp (requests.Response): The HTTP response object.

Returns: * str | None: The classified refusal category string (e.g., "content_policy_violation", "moderation", "safety"), or None if the response is not a moderation rejection.

Example: 

def _refusal_category(resp) -> str | None:
    if resp.status_code != 403:
        return None
    err = _error_body(resp)
    meta = err.get("metadata") or {}
    kind = str(err.get("type") or err.get("error_type") or meta.get("error_type") or "").lower()
    if kind in _REFUSAL_ERROR_TYPES:
        return kind
    if meta.get("reasons") or meta.get("flagged_input"):
        reasons = meta.get("reasons") or ["moderation"]
        return ",".join(map(str, reasons)) if isinstance(reasons, list) else str(reasons)
    return None

This classification allows the orchestrator to differentiate permanent policy blocks from retryable network or auth errors.

docs.title: _post()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _post(url: str, headers: dict, payload: dict) -> requests.Response:

Description: Dispatches an HTTP POST request to the OpenRouter chat completions endpoint with bounded retry handling for transient errors. It configures connect and read timeouts, manages exponential backoffs, respects server-side Retry-After headers, and intercepts moderation refusals before surfacing fatal exceptions.

The method operates in two distinct phases:

docs.title: Phase 1: Transient Retry Loop & Timeout Configuration
docs.text:
for attempt in range(1, _MAX_ATTEMPTS + 1):
    try:
        resp = requests.post(url, headers=headers, json=payload, stream=True, timeout=(15, _read_timeout()))
    except (requests.exceptions.ConnectionError, requests.exceptions.Timeout) as e:
        if attempt == _MAX_ATTEMPTS:
            raise RuntimeError(f"OpenRouter request failed after {attempt} attempts: {e}") from e
        time.sleep(2**attempt)
        continue
In this phase, the request is executed with a 15-second connect timeout and a streaming read timeout derived from _read_timeout(). Low-level socket timeouts or connection drops trigger exponential backoff sleep cycles (2**attempt seconds) up to _MAX_ATTEMPTS (3 attempts).

docs.title: Phase 2: Response Status Inspection & Refusal Trapping
docs.text:
if resp.status_code in _RETRYABLE_STATUS and attempt < _MAX_ATTEMPTS:
        wait = min(_retry_after(resp) or 2**attempt * 2, 60)
        emit_raw("WARNING", f"OpenRouter HTTP {resp.status_code}; retrying in {wait:.0f}s ({_error_detail(resp)})", dest="LOG")
        resp.close()
        time.sleep(wait)
        continue
    if resp.status_code >= 400:
        detail, category = _error_detail(resp), _refusal_category(resp)
        resp.close()
        if category:
            model = payload.get("model", "")
            count_event("OPENROUTER", "refusals")
            emit("WARN_LLM_REFUSAL", provider="OpenRouter", model=model, category=category)
            emit_raw("WARNING", f"OpenRouter HTTP 403 refusal: {detail}", dest="LOG")
            raise LLMRefusalError(model, category, provider="OPENROUTER")
        raise RuntimeError(f"OpenRouter HTTP {resp.status_code}: {detail}")
    return resp
raise RuntimeError("OpenRouter request failed")  # unreachable
HTTP status codes in _RETRYABLE_STATUS ({408, 429, 502, 503, 524, 529}) close the response and trigger delayed retries using the Retry-After header or exponential backoff capped at 60 seconds. For non-retryable 4xx/5xx status codes, the response is inspected via _refusal_category(); if identified as a moderation rejection, an LLMRefusalError is raised immediately. Otherwise, a generic RuntimeError terminates the attempt.

Parameters: * url (str): The complete endpoint URL. * headers (dict): HTTP headers including authorization and content type. * payload (dict): The serialized request payload.

Returns: * requests.Response: An open streaming response object.

Raises: * LLMRefusalError: When an HTTP 403 status indicates a content policy refusal. * RuntimeError: When network attempts are exhausted or non-retryable HTTP errors are returned.

Example: 

resp = _post(
    url="https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions",
    headers={"Authorization": "Bearer sk-or-..."},
    payload={"model": "openai/gpt-4o", "stream": True},
)

docs.title: _consume()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _consume(resp: requests.Response) -> dict:

Description: Parses the incoming HTTP response, reading and assembling Server-Sent Events (SSE) into text, reasoning blocks, finish reasons, and usage metrics. The function handles both standard SSE streaming lines and monolithic non-streamed JSON bodies returned by proxies that ignore the "stream": true parameter.

The parsing implementation is split across two logical phases:

docs.title: Phase 1: Stream Header Inspection & Non-SSE Fallback
docs.text:
out = {"text": [], "reasoning": [], "finish": None, "native": None, "refusal": None, "usage": None, "events": 0}
try:
    if "application/json" in (resp.headers.get("Content-Type") or "").lower():
        # An OpenAI-compatible proxy that ignores stream=true answers with one JSON body.
        _apply_chunk(out, resp.json())
The state accumulator dictionary is initialized with empty buffers for content fragments. The helper inspects the Content-Type header: if the server responded with monolithic application/json rather than text/event-stream, it decodes the payload in a single pass via _apply_chunk().

docs.title: Phase 2: Line-by-Line SSE Decoding & Keep-Alive Filtering
docs.text:
else:
        for raw_line in resp.iter_lines():
            line = raw_line.decode("utf-8", errors="replace") if isinstance(raw_line, bytes) else raw_line
            if not line or line.startswith(":") or not line.startswith("data:"):
                continue  # blank separators and ': OPENROUTER PROCESSING' keep-alives
            data = line[5:].strip()
            if data == "[DONE]":
                break
            try:
                chunk = json.loads(data)
            except ValueError:
                continue
            _apply_chunk(out, chunk)
finally:
    resp.close()
out["text"] = "".join(out["text"])
out["reasoning"] = "".join(out["reasoning"])
return out
For streaming responses, the method reads raw byte lines via resp.iter_lines(). Each line is decoded individually using utf-8 with replacement fallbacks (avoiding splitlines() bugs with U+2028 and U+0085 control characters). Lines containing keep-alives (: OPENROUTER PROCESSING) or empty separators are skipped. JSON data chunks are parsed and folded into the accumulator until the [DONE] event is encountered. The response is guaranteed to close in a finally block before accumulated strings are joined and returned.

Parameters: * resp (requests.Response): The active HTTP streaming response.

Returns: * dict: An aggregated stream dictionary containing merged text, reasoning, termination reasons, and token usage metrics.

Example: 

result = _consume(resp)
print(f"Consumed {result['events']} chunks, text length: {len(result['text'])}")

docs.title: _apply_chunk()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _apply_chunk(out: dict, chunk: dict) -> None:

Description: Updates the running accumulator dictionary with data extracted from a single SSE event or completion chunk. It increments the total event count, raises exceptions on inline stream errors, stores token usage objects, and appends incoming content or reasoning deltas to their respective lists.

Parameters: * out (dict): The target accumulator dictionary modified in-place. * chunk (dict): The parsed JSON chunk received over the wire.

Raises: * RuntimeError: If the chunk or choice object contains an upstream error structure.

Example: 

def _apply_chunk(out: dict, chunk: dict) -> None:
    out["events"] += 1
    if chunk.get("error"):
        err = chunk["error"]
        raise RuntimeError(f"OpenRouter stream error: {err.get('message', err) if isinstance(err, dict) else err}")
    if chunk.get("usage"):
        out["usage"] = chunk["usage"]
    for choice in chunk.get("choices") or []:
        delta = choice.get("delta") or choice.get("message") or {}
        if delta.get("content"):
            out["text"].append(delta["content"])
        if delta.get("reasoning"):
            out["reasoning"].append(delta["reasoning"])
        if delta.get("refusal"):
            out["refusal"] = delta["refusal"]
        if choice.get("finish_reason"):
            out["finish"] = choice["finish_reason"]
        if choice.get("native_finish_reason"):
            out["native"] = choice["native_finish_reason"]
        if choice.get("error"):
            err = choice["error"]
            raise RuntimeError(f"OpenRouter upstream error: {err.get('message', err) if isinstance(err, dict) else err}")

This helper abstracts schema differences between streaming delta payloads (choice["delta"]) and static completion payloads (choice["message"]).

docs.title: _record()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _record(model: str, result: dict, raw_prompt_tokens: int, desc: str, elapsed: float, generation_id: str | None) -> None:

Description: Parses reported token usage, calculates actual inference costs (accounting for Bring-Your-Own-Key deployments), publishes metrics to the central usage ledger in llm_common.py, and registers observed token counts with token_utils.py for ratio calibration.

The recording logic is executed across two distinct phases:

docs.title: Phase 1: Token Metric Extraction & BYOK Cost Calculation
docs.text:
if not result["usage"]:
    # No usage chunk (dropped stream, or a proxy that omits usage): a request, but unmeasured.
    record_usage("OPENROUTER", model, cost=None, measured=False)
    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"OPENROUTER USAGE | model={model} | no usage reported | generation_id={generation_id or 'n/a'}", dest="BOTH")
    return
usage = result["usage"]
prompt = usage.get("prompt_tokens") or 0
completion = usage.get("completion_tokens") or 0  # includes reasoning tokens
reasoning_tokens = (usage.get("completion_tokens_details") or {}).get("reasoning_tokens") or 0
details = usage.get("prompt_tokens_details") or {}
cached = details.get("cached_tokens") or 0
cache_write = details.get("cache_write_tokens") or 0
cost = usage.get("cost")
upstream = (usage.get("cost_details") or {}).get("upstream_inference_cost")
if usage.get("is_byok") and isinstance(upstream, int | float):
    # BYOK: `cost` is only OpenRouter's fee; the provider bills upstream_inference_cost to your key.
    cost = (cost if isinstance(cost, int | float) else 0.0) + upstream
If usage was omitted from the stream, the call is marked as unmeasured. When usage data is present, the function extracts input, output, reasoning, and cache metrics. If Bring-Your-Own-Key (is_byok) routing is detected, OpenRouter's routing fee is combined with upstream_inference_cost to reflect total cost.

docs.title: Phase 2: Token Ledger Recording & Heuristic Calibration
docs.text:
record_usage(
    "OPENROUTER",
    model,
    input_tokens=prompt,
    output_tokens=completion,
    thinking_tokens=reasoning_tokens,
    cache_read=cached,
    cache_write=cache_write,
    cost=float(cost) if isinstance(cost, int | float) else None,
)
ratio = prompt / raw_prompt_tokens if raw_prompt_tokens else 0.0
from utils.token_utils import observe_prompt_tokens

observe_prompt_tokens("OPENROUTER", model, raw_prompt_tokens, prompt)
emit_raw(
    "DEBUG",
    f"OPENROUTER USAGE | model={model} | {desc} | finish={result['finish']} (native={result['native']}) | in={prompt:,} | out={completion:,} | "
    f"reasoning={reasoning_tokens:,} | cached={cached:,} | cost={'$' + format(cost, '.4f') if isinstance(cost, int | float) else 'n/a'} | "
    f"elapsed={elapsed:.1f}s | observed_token_ratio={ratio:.2f} | generation_id={generation_id or 'n/a'}",
    dest="BOTH",
)
The metrics are committed to record_usage(). The prompt token count is then compared with raw_prompt_tokens to calibrate the runtime heuristic tokenizer ratio via observe_prompt_tokens(). Detailed diagnostic telemetry is written to log destinations.

Parameters: * model (str): The model identifier. * result (dict): The dictionary compiled by _consume(). * raw_prompt_tokens (int): Baseline tiktoken count for the prompt. * desc (str): Diagnostic parameter description. * elapsed (float): Total round-trip latency in seconds. * generation_id (str | None): OpenRouter generation ID extracted from X-Generation-Id.

Example: 

_record(
    model="anthropic/claude-3.7-sonnet",
    result=consumed_result,
    raw_prompt_tokens=1542,
    desc="effort=high",
    elapsed=12.4,
    generation_id="gen-abc123xyz",
)

docs.title: Module Constants Reference
docs.text:
The following module-level constants define transport bounds, reasoning token budgets, and refusal patterns:

Identifier Type Value / Scope Description _RETRYABLE_STATUS set[int] {408, 429, 502, 503, 524, 529} HTTP status codes that trigger automatic transient backoff retries. _MAX_ATTEMPTS int 3 Maximum number of attempts allowed for transient HTTP connection failures. _REFUSAL_NATIVE_REASONS set[str] {"refusal", "safety", "prohibited_content", "recitation", "blocklist", "spii", "content_filter"} Upstream native stop indicators classified as provider refusals or policy blocks. _DETERMINISTIC_NATIVE_REASONS set[str] {"refusal", "prohibited_content", "blocklist", "spii"} Non-retryable refusal reasons that persistently fail for the same input prompt. _REFUSAL_ERROR_TYPES set[str] {"refusal", "content_policy_violation", "moderation"} Error type identifiers in HTTP 403 responses that indicate moderation blocks. _REASONING_BUDGETS dict[str, int] {"minimal": 1024, "low": 2048, "medium": 8192, "high": 16384, "xhigh": 24576, "max": 32000} Integer thinking token budgets assigned when models support max_tokens but not categorical efforts. _APP_TITLE str "Codebase Knowledge Builder" Application title transmitted in attribution headers when OPENROUTER_APP_URL is set.

docs.title: OpenRouterRequestPayload
docs.text:
The JSON dictionary assembled by build_payload() and transmitted over HTTP to /v1/chat/completions:

Field Type Required Description model str Yes Target OpenRouter model identifier (e.g., "openai/gpt-4o"). messages list[dict[str, str]] Yes Array of chat messages, formatted as [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}]. stream bool Yes Always set to True to enforce SSE streaming transport. max_tokens int No Bounded completion ceiling derived from catalog context length minus input tokens. reasoning dict No Nested dictionary configuring model-specific reasoning behaviour. temperature float No Sampling temperature (defaults to 0.7); omitted if reasoning is enabled or rejected.

Example Structure: 

{
  "model": "anthropic/claude-3.7-sonnet",
  "messages": [
    {"role": "user", "content": "Analyze system architecture"}
  ],
  "stream": true,
  "max_tokens": 16384,
  "reasoning": {
    "effort": "high",
    "exclude": true
  }
}

docs.title: ReasoningConfig
docs.text:
The schema of the nested "reasoning" dictionary placed inside the request payload:

Field Type Required Description effort str Optional Categorical reasoning effort level (e.g., "low", "medium", "high"). max_tokens int Optional Fixed integer token budget for models that only support numeric reasoning budgets. exclude bool Yes Set to True during standard runs to omit raw reasoning chains from response payloads, or False in debug mode.

docs.title: StreamResult
docs.text:
The internal dictionary compiled by _consume() representing aggregated stream data:

Field Type Description text str The complete decoded assistant response text merged across all stream chunks. reasoning str Accumulated chain-of-thought text (empty unless running in debug mode or if returned unredacted). finish str \| None Standard OpenAI completion finish reason (e.g., "stop", "length", "content_filter"). native str \| None Upstream provider-specific native finish reason (e.g., "recitation", "safety"). refusal str \| None Text or code populated if the model returned an explicit refusal field. usage dict \| None The raw usage dictionary returned in the final SSE event. events int Total count of SSE data chunks parsed during the stream session.

docs.text:

docs.title: Notable Error Patterns and Resolution Rules
docs.text:
1. Transient Network and Gateway Failures: Connection errors, socket read timeouts, and HTTP status codes defined in _RETRYABLE_STATUS (408, 429, 502, 503, 524, 529) do not immediately terminate execution. _post() executes up to 3 attempts. When a server returns a Retry-After header, the client pauses for the indicated duration (capped at 60 seconds); otherwise, it applies exponential backoff delays (2**attempt * 2).

  2. HTTP 403 Moderation Rejection vs Authentication Errors: Standard HTTP 403 Forbidden errors can signify either an invalid API key or an upstream content moderation rejection. _refusal_category() inspects the error payload's type and metadata.reasons fields. If flagged as a policy violation, moderation block, or guardrail refusal, it raises LLMRefusalError(retryable=False). Unmatched 403 responses raise a standard RuntimeError.

  3. Stream Disconnection and Incomplete Outputs: If an SSE stream terminates without emitting a final finish_reason (e.g., due to an interrupted connection or proxy termination), the module rejects the accumulated text buffer and raises a RuntimeError. This prevents partial completions from entering downstream processing stages.

  4. Stochastic vs. Deterministic Refusals: In call_openrouter(), completion refusals are bifurcated:

  5. Deterministic Refusals: Explicit model refusals or stops matching _DETERMINISTIC_NATIVE_REASONS ("refusal", "prohibited_content", "blocklist", "spii") raise LLMRefusalError(retryable=False). Upstream callers cache these refusals and avoid redundant retry attempts.

  6. Stochastic Refusals: Terminations triggered by candidate sampling filters ("content_filter", "safety", "recitation") raise LLMRefusalError(retryable=True), allowing the orchestrator to retry the prompt with different sampling conditions.

  7. Cache-Protection via Sentinel Types: When a generation terminates with finish_reason == "length", the function wraps the accumulated text in a TruncatedResponse instance (subclassed from str). Upstream caching layers in call_llm.py detect this sentinel type and bypass disk caching, preventing corrupted or cut-off outputs from persisting.

docs.title: mkdocs.py
docs.text: Source: utils/mkdocs.py

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
Following the Large Language Model provider execution harnesses such as utils/llm_openrouter.py, the utils/mkdocs.py module acts as the downstream static site compilation, structural organization, and filesystem persistence engine of the pipeline. While the LLM inference layers generate decoupled markdown chapters and chapter-level abstractions, mkdocs.py orchestrates the conversion of these discrete text artifacts into a cohesive, production-ready static documentation website powered by MkDocs Material, or alternatively into a consolidated standalone Markdown archive.

The module provides full lifecycle management for documentation generation. It constructs strict MkDocs configurations (mkdocs.yml) equipped with search, code copy capabilities, custom-themed Mermaid diagram renderers, and panzoom interactivity. For complex API reference projects containing numerous modules, it optionally engages an LLM-driven semantic clustering pipeline to group source files into logical sections and sub-packages. Furthermore, it enforces deterministic post-processing routines that sanitize YAML strings, normalize cross-chapter Markdown hyperlinks across nested directories, and prune stale files from previous compilation passes using filesystem inode identity matching.

docs.title: build_mkdocs_config()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def build_mkdocs_config(site_name: str, nav_yaml: str, include_home: bool = True, lang_code: str = "") -> str:

Description: Constructs the complete text of an mkdocs.yml configuration file configured for the Material for MkDocs theme. The generated configuration embeds syntax highlighting via pymdownx.highlight, Mermaid diagram rendering via custom fences, diagram zoom and pan capabilities via panzoom, search extensions, dynamic navigation layouts, and localized user interface settings.

Parameters: * site_name (str): The primary site title displayed in the header and metadata. * nav_yaml (str): The raw YAML string representing the MkDocs nav block. * include_home (bool): Whether to inject a top-level home navigation link pointing to index.md. Defaults to True. * lang_code (str): Optional two-letter language code (such as "vi", "zh", "ja") for MkDocs Material theme UI localization. Defaults to "".

Returns: * str: A formatted YAML string ready to be written to mkdocs.yml.

Raises: * This function does not raise internal exceptions; invalid strings are safely formatted using scalar quoting.

Example: 

# Extracted from write_mkdocs_output in utils/mkdocs.py
language = prep_res.get("language", "english")
lang_code = lang_code_map.get(language.lower(), "")
mkdocs_config = build_mkdocs_config(site_title, nav_snippet, include_home=True, lang_code=lang_code)
mkdocs_filepath = os.path.join(output_path, "mkdocs.yml")
with open(mkdocs_filepath, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    f.write(mkdocs_config)

The core implementation handles YAML scalar normalization, theme palettes, Markdown extensions, and Mermaid integration:

def build_mkdocs_config(site_name: str, nav_yaml: str, include_home: bool = True, lang_code: str = "") -> str:
    # Extract nav items from nav_snippet (strip the "nav:" header line)
    nav_lines = nav_yaml.split("\n")
    nav_body = "\n".join(nav_lines[1:]) if nav_lines else ""

    # Optional Home nav entry (write_mkdocs_output always writes docs/index.md and passes include_home=True)
    home_line = f"  - {yaml_str(get('UI_HOME'))}: index.md\n" if include_home else ""

    # Optional Material theme language (e.g. "vi", "zh", "ja", "ko")
    lang_line = f"  language: {lang_code}\n" if lang_code else ""

    return (
        f"site_name: {yaml_str(site_name)}\n"
        f"theme:\n"
        f"  name: material\n"
        f"{lang_line}"
        f"  features:\n"
        f"    - content.code.copy\n"
        f"    - navigation.indexes\n"
        f"  palette:\n"
        f"    - scheme: default\n"
        f"      toggle:\n"
        f"        icon: material/brightness-7\n"
        f"        name: Switch to dark mode\n"
        f"    - scheme: slate\n"
        f"      toggle:\n"
        f"        icon: material/brightness-4\n"
        f"        name: Switch to light mode\n"
        f"plugins:\n"
        f"  - search\n"
        f"  - panzoom:\n"
        f"      include_selectors:\n"
        f"        - '.mermaid-raw'\n"
        f"      exclude_selectors:\n"
        f"        - '.mermaid'\n"
        f"markdown_extensions:\n"
        f"  - pymdownx.highlight:\n"
        f"      anchor_linenums: true\n"
        f"      use_pygments: true\n"
        f"  - pymdownx.superfences:\n"
        f"      custom_fences:\n"
        f"        - name: mermaid\n"
        f"          class: mermaid-raw\n"
        f"          format: !!python/name:pymdownx.superfences.fence_div_format\n"
        f"  - pymdownx.inlinehilite\n"
        f"extra_javascript:\n"
        f"  - https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mermaid@11/dist/mermaid.min.js\n"
        f"  - javascripts/mermaid-init.js\n"
        f"nav:\n"
        f"{home_line}"
        f"{nav_body}\n"
    )

The function strips the root nav: key from the input YAML snippet to allow clean indentation nesting under the global nav: block. It configures the pymdownx.superfences extension using fence_div_format to emit <div class="mermaid-raw"> wrappers for diagrams instead of default preformatted code blocks. This naming convention explicitly bypasses Material for MkDocs' internal color scheme overrides while permitting the panzoom plugin to bind to the outer <div>.
